sentences.text:
Facts in brief are that the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 for compensation of Rs. 4,60,000/- submitting that he sustained injuries in motor accident on 07-11-2020 at 7:00 PM by negligent driving by car vehicle No. MP21-CA-5018, owned by respondent No. 2 and insured by respondent No.3.
He was treated for the injuries but, sustained permanent physical disability.

He was aged 34 years and by profession of driving he earns Rs.
9,000/- per month and now his earning has been effected.
3. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 did not appear and respondent No.3 contested the case on various grounds including the breach of policy.
The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence of S.K. Tiwari (PW-1) and admitted documents Ex.P/1 to Ex. P/17.
The respondent did not examine any witness.

4. The Tribunal found proved that the appellant sustained grievous injuries by negligent driving of offending vehicle No. MP21-CA-5018 but, did not found proved that the appellant suffered permanent physical disability.

It was also found proved that the vehicle was owned by the respondent No.2 and insured by the respondent No.3 and awarded a total sum of Rs. 33,592/- in the following heads:-
 (a) Medical expenses : Rs.
 (b) Conveyance, nutrition diet and : Rs. 
 pain and suffering -------------------------------------------------------------------------

This appeal has been preferred on the ground that the Tribunal passed a meager amount without looking to the material available on record, it ought to have awarded suitable compensation for medical expenses.
Tribunal ought to have found proved that due to fracture in right leg, the appellant suffered permanent disability.
The Tribunal ought to have awarded in the head of loss of future income.

6. Heard.
7.
Learned counsel for respondent No. 3 opposed the prayer.

8. Perused the record.
9.
The findings of the Tribunal in paragraphs- 14 and 15 are proper that appellant suffered grievous injuries but, did not cause permanent physical disability.
Medical expenses head have been taken into consideration and nothing has been left.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has not taken into consideration that the during treatment the appellant suffered loss of income.

Considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment as depicted from Ex.
P/17, a total loss of two months income is proper.
So, the appellant is awarded Rs. 15,000/- for the loss of two months of income during treatment.
The second head of amount is on the lower side.

Rs.
10,000/- is further enhanced in the second head of paragraph-26 of the award.

11. The appeal is partly allowed and a total sum of Rs. 25,000/- is further enhanced with interest @
6% from the date of application i.e. 04-01- 2021.
